title: A small family of stratum-product and subobject models for integral constructible sheaves
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention], with schemes and scalar coefficient rings in $\mathcal U$, small site skeletons and module sections in $\mathcal V$. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and put $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules mean sheaves of $R_T$-modules on the fixed small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A finite constant local model on $T$ means a module pro-étale locally isomorphic to $R_U\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_E}}\underline P$, with $P$ a finitely presented scalar $\mathcal O_E$-module [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. There is a $\mathcal V$-small set of representative such sheaves $\{F_{T,t}\}_{t\in I_T}$ for every stratum $T$ of every finite locally closed scheme stratification of $X$ [def-constructible-stratification]. Let $J$ index all pairs consisting of a finite stratification $(a_s:S_s\hookrightarrow X)_{s<n}$ within the fixed scheme bound and a tuple $(t_s\in I_{S_s})_{s<n}$. Then $J$ is a $\mathcal V$-small set. For $j$ given by this pair put $P_j=\prod_{s<n}a_{s*}F_{S_s,t_s}$, using the module adjunctions $a_s^*\dashv a_{s*}$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For every constructible $R_X$-module $C$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible] there are $j\in J$ and isomorphisms $\varphi_s:a_s^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{S_s,t_s}$ such that the map $u:C\to P_j$ with components $a_{s*}(\varphi_s)\circ\eta_{s,C}$ is a monomorphism, where $\eta_s$ is the adjunction unit. For each $j$, subobjects of $P_j$, up to isomorphism over $P_j$, are represented by a $\mathcal V$-small set of image subsheaves; each image is specified by a family of subsets of $P_j(V)$ indexed by objects $V$ of the small site. Thus the family of all these image subsheaves, for all $j\in J$, is $\mathcal V$-small. The empty stratification is allowed when $X$ is empty, with product the zero module sheaf.

proof.text: For any stratum $T$, work on its fixed $\mathcal V$-small site. This site has terminal object $T/T$ and finite limits: for $U\to W\leftarrow V$ over $T$, both arrows are weakly étale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], so $U\times_WV\to T$ is weakly étale by base change and composition. These scheme fibre products exist by [def-pc-fibre-product] and satisfy the same universal property in the full site category. Products are fibre products over $T$; the equalizer of $a,b:U\rightrightarrows V$ is $U\times_{V\times_TV}V$, using $(a,b)$ and the diagonal. Thus the same construction gives equalizers and finite limits. The bounded skeleton retains these limits up to isomorphism, by [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 098M, lemma-fibre-products-proetale: explicit terminal-object, fibre-product and equalizer construction

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$. The scalar presentation codes form the set $Q=\coprod_{m,n\in\mathbf N}\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(A)$ in $\mathcal U$, hence in $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. For a code $q:A^m\to A^n$, take the actual quotient module $P_q=A^n/\operatorname{im}q$. By [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], every finitely presented scalar module is isomorphic to some $P_q$: its given surjection $A^n\to P$ factors through this quotient, and the induced map is surjective with zero kernel. Consequently the modules $B_{U,q}=R_U\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{P_q}$ provide a small family of the scalar models in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] on every site object $U$. Passing an isomorphism $P\cong P_q$ through constant sheaves and tensor extension gives an isomorphism of these models; no assertion about arbitrary matrices of coefficient sections is used.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence: finite stratifications, finite scalar presentations, small-site local models and gluing morphisms

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to each site object $U\to T$: $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is the slice $T_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$, with the same coverings. Clause (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies inverse image of any ring sheaf with slice restriction. Combining it with [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies $R_T|_U$ with $R_U$, including its scalar constant-section map. Hence the families $B_{U,q}$ of step 2 are sheaves over precisely the restricted ring required by [lem-sfb-locally-prescribed-modules-small]. Apply that lemma on the site of step 1 with $I_U=Q$. For a module $M$ on $T$, the module pullback $M|_U$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] has underlying sheaf the inverse image, with action through the cartesian coefficient isomorphism (last paragraph of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]), and clause (1) identifies that inverse image with the slice restriction. So the lemma's class is exactly the finite constant local model sheaves of the item, since the covers and scalar models agree. Its representative family consists of members of this class; denote it $(F_{T,t})_{t\in I_T}$, with $I_T\in\mathcal V$. All sites and section sets have the required size. The strata within the fixed scheme bound form a set in $\mathcal V$, so choose these representative families simultaneously, using set-indexed choice in an ambient universe containing $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence: finite stratifications, finite scalar presentations, small-site local models and gluing morphisms

proof.text: A finite stratification is a finite list of schemes in the fixed bound and immersions to $X$ subject to the disjointness and covering conditions of [def-constructible-stratification]. Schemes and their morphisms in this bound have set-sized codes in $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]; a finite list is therefore in a $\mathcal V$-small set, and imposing these conditions takes a subset. Call that set $H$. For $h\in H$ let its strata be $(S_s)_{s<n(h)}$. Then $J=\coprod_{h\in H}\prod_{s<n(h)}I_{S_s}$ is in $\mathcal V$, by closure under small sums and finite products. This is exactly the indexing set asserted in the statement, including all choices of stratum representatives.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence: finite stratifications, finite scalar presentations, small-site local models and gluing morphisms

proof.text: For $j=(h,(t_s)_s)$ the functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] put every $a_{s*}F_{S_s,t_s}$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ and specify the adjunction units used in the item. These functors, and constructibility, are defined on the internal module objects $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}$; by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] that category is equivalent to the sectionwise module sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the section-ring sheaf of $R_T$, by a functor keeping underlying abelian sheaves, sections and restriction maps, and $\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ below means either through it. These categories are abelian, with kernels computed sectionwise, by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] to the finite discrete diagram of these direct images: it gives the product $P_j$ in that category, with $P_j(V)=\prod_{s<n(h)}(a_{s*}F_{S_s,t_s})(V)$. The section sets lie in $\mathcal V$; the empty product is the zero module sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, limits paragraph; Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; module adjunctions as fixed in the statement

proof.text: Let $C$ be constructible. Its defining finite stratification in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] has finite constant local models on each stratum. Since $X$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, it is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] gives quasi-separatedness. Thus $X$ is qcqs and the finite-stratification clause of that definition applies. Choose that stratification $h\in H$. For each of its finitely many strata, the representative property proved in step 3 supplies $t_s\in I_{S_s}$ and an isomorphism $\varphi_s:a_s^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{S_s,t_s}$. Thus these choices define $j\in J$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence: finite stratifications, finite scalar presentations, small-site local models and gluing morphisms

proof.text: Each $a_s^*$ is exact and its underlying abelian sheaf is the inverse image along $a_s$, by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]; it is additive and preserves kernels. The restrictions $a_s^*$ jointly detect zero objects: apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] to the given finite stratification and the identity pro-étale covering on each stratum. Its Noetherian hypothesis is exactly quasi-compactness and local Noetherianity, both assumed for $X$; its arbitrary-ring-sheaf conclusion applies to $R_X$, identified with $R_{S_s}$ after inverse image by the cartesian coefficient isomorphism. Now apply [lem-sfb-joint-adjunction-model-embedding] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, $\mathcal B_s=\operatorname{Mod}(R_{S_s})$, $F_s=a_s^*$, $G_s=a_{s*}$, $M=C$, $B_s=F_{S_s,t_s}$ and $e_s=\varphi_s$. The abelian categories, adjunctions and product were verified in step 5. It follows that the map $u:C\to P_j$ whose components are $a_{s*}(\varphi_s)\circ\eta_{s,C}$ is a monomorphism, with exactly the units specified in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence: finite stratifications, finite scalar presentations, small-site local models and gluing morphisms

proof.text: Fix $j$ and a subobject represented by a monomorphism $m:M\to P_j$. Its kernel arrow is zero, by cancellation against the zero arrow. Since kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every $m_V$ is injective. Put $N(V)=m_V(M(V))\subseteq P_j(V)$. Linearity and naturality make these subsets submodules stable under restriction. The bijections $M(V)\to N(V)$ commute with restrictions and scalar actions; transporting the sheaf axiom through these bijections makes $N$ a module sheaf, and gives an isomorphism $M\cong N$ over $P_j$. This is the sectionwise image for a mono; no assertion that the sectionwise image of an arbitrary sheaf morphism is already a sheaf is being made. If two such monos have equal families $N(V)$, their induced isomorphisms to $N$ identify them over $P_j$. Conversely an isomorphism over $P_j$ gives the same subsets at every $V$.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; explicit sectionwise kernel and image argument for monomorphisms

proof.text: Let $K$ be the object set of the fixed small site of $X$. The family of subsets specifying an image in step 8 is an element of $D_j=\prod_{V\in K}\mathcal P(P_j(V))$. Both $K$ and the section sets are in $\mathcal V$, so $D_j\in\mathcal V$ by [def-weil-size-convention]. Take the subset $E_j\subseteq D_j$ consisting of families that form module subsheaves of $P_j$. The inherited operations and restrictions determine a unique module subsheaf from each such family. Each is itself an image, namely the image of its inclusion. Step 8 therefore represents all subobjects, up to isomorphism over $P_j$, by this small family of actual image subsheaves. Finally $\coprod_{j\in J}E_j\in\mathcal V$, giving the required small family simultaneously for all $j$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence: finite stratifications, finite scalar presentations, small-site local models and gluing morphisms

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, the empty list is a stratification by [def-constructible-stratification], and its tuple of indices is the unique empty tuple. The empty cover of the empty scheme is a pro-étale cover by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The sheaf axiom forces every module sheaf on that site to be zero: every site object over $X$ is empty, and its empty covering has exactly one matching family. Thus the map to the empty product of step 5 is $0\to0$, which is monic, and this product has exactly one image subsheaf. The same argument handles empty strata in any chosen stratification; zero scalar models, including the $m=n=0$ presentation, were already allowed in step 2.
